top_choice_rationale: P002 (B001, Grossman and Helpman) is a mature, roughly thirty-year-old contribution with clean two-person attribution. It put organised-interest influence on trade policy into an explicit equilibrium model, which gave empirical work a precise object to estimate. Its main weakness is a mixed empirical record for protection-for-sale, so its case rests on framework influence more than on settled confirmation. I rank P001 (B020) a close second because its empirical footprint is wider, but its credit boundary with Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum is unresolved and cannot be repaired within the credited list. P004 follows for its design-based evidence, offset by debates over magnitude and persistence and by an attribution question over the task-theory strand. P003 is placed fourth because its identification of constitutional effects is weaker, the credit between the Persson-Tabellini and Besley-Persson strands is hard to separate, and it overlaps with the 2024 prize. I still prefer P003 to making no award, so P000 is last. This ranking does not count first-place support as merit.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile for P002, P001 or P004. P003 (B016) is adjacent to my field of political institutions and quality of government, and I gave the 2024 presentation speech on institutions and prosperity. That speech was delivered for the Academy and does not establish a private preference. My profile lists a Governance paper co-authored with a 'Persson'. It does not say which Persson, and I have not verified that this is not Torsten Persson, who is credited on B016. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
